summary: IPR defense by a patent owner at the PTAB (35 U.S.C. §§311-319), from the Patent Owner Preliminary Response through a final written decision, with appeal to the CAFC.
notes: Protagonist is the PATENT OWNER defending against a petitioner's inter partes review, not the petitioner. Uses `ptab-patent-trial-appeal-board` + `cafc` (links.json's `cafc@ptab` instance supplies the appeal, remanding only back to the Board). `start` is set to `popr-window` (POPR clock start) so the graph begins where the patent owner's own defense choices begin, skipping the pre-suit/petition-filing steps that are the petitioner's decisions, not the defense's. JUDGMENT CALL (perspective mapping): this pack's actor vocabulary (schemaVersion 2 as of a later migration, but `roles` is still just the default identity mapping — applicant→self, examiner/office→nature, either→nature; the pack has no dedicated patent-owner actor) uses `applicant` for the PETITIONER's moves (files the petition, moves for joinder, replies, opposes amendment — verified against every `actor: applicant` edge in the pack) and buckets the patent owner's own moves (file/waive POPR, file/skip response, settle, move to amend, waive oral argument, request rehearing/Director review, decide whether to appeal) together with genuinely joint/neutral steps under one `either` actor — the pack has no actor distinguishing 'patent owner's own choice' from 'joint/neutral event'. `perspective` below remaps `applicant -> opponent` (the petitioner becomes the adversary we solve against) and `either -> self` (so the patent owner's actual defense choices are exposed to `explain`/`solve`), leaving `examiner`/`office` at their default `nature` (the Board and the Federal Circuit acting adjudicatively). This is the closest reading the CURRENT pack data supports without editing pack content (out of this scenario's scope); it necessarily also treats some genuinely joint/neutral `either` edges as 'our' choice — flagged here rather than silently assumed. A cleaner fix (a dedicated `patent-owner` actor in the pack) is a pack-content change for whoever owns `packs/ptab-patent-trial-appeal-board.json` next, not this scenario. SECOND JUDGMENT CALL (payoffs): several CAFC-side and post-FWD PTAB terminals (`appeal-forfeited-unappealed`, `cafc@ptab::window-blown-ptab`/`dismissed-failure-to-prosecute`/`rule36-affirmance`/`affirmed`/`dismissed-jurisdictional-defect`/`cert-not-sought`/`cert-denied`/`cert-granted`) are reachable regardless of which prior FWD outcome preceded them — a known engine/pack-content limitation (docs/CRITIQUE.md, 'Markov on the node': the graph has no memory of which FWD led here). Rather than inventing false precision, this scenario assigns those a flat mid-range illustrative value ($1,500,000, half of the $3,000,000 illustrative patent value used for a clean win) and says so per-terminal below instead of leaving it unstated. All dollar figures assume an illustrative $3,000,000 patent value (this patent's licensing/enforcement value if it survives intact) and a $700/hr blended rate; neither is sourced (no real matter identified) — override both per actual matter.
